name: Apoliticism
summary: Apoliticism is apathy or antipathy toward political affiliation: the apolitical person is uninterested in or uninvolved with politics, or claims a politically neutral, unbiased position. Historic forms include Epicurean withdrawal from public life for the sake of tranquility, and Anabaptist separation of the believing community from the state. It is a stance about participation, not a programme, so it says little about most policy questions.
scope: Apoliticism as a stance of withdrawal or neutrality, drawing on Epicurus (Principal Doctrines), the Anabaptist Schleitheim Confession, and the modern apolitical or apathetic citizen as described in reference works. It excludes partisan 'centrism' and organised abstentionist movements, and nearly all policy answers are inferred or neutral.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Withdrawal from politics gives no view on health-care provision; adherents are split between indifference and Epicurean self-reliance.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is an ordinary party-political dispute that apolitical people decline to take a side on.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Apoliticism takes no side in the market-versus-state contest, so this is a split inference.

public-ownership.rationale: Ownership of utilities is a partisan economic question the stance is indifferent to.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax levels are a standard partisan fight; withdrawal means no committed position.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are a political actor; apolitical adherents neither champion nor oppose them.

property-fundamental.rationale: Epicurus treats rights as useful compacts, not absolutes, but apoliticism has no property doctrine.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare cuts are a partisan question; no apolitical doctrine settles it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is a culture-war issue apolitical people avoid taking sides on.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech regulation is a contested political question with no apolitical doctrine.

state-harmful.rationale: Epicureans avoided politics but accepted the state as a useful compact for security (KD 6, 31), so they stop short of calling it harmful.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

reviewHistory.rationale: Security funding is a partisan matter; adherents are split, though KD 6 values security from others.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A moral-political dispute with no apolitical position.

traditional-family.rationale: A culture-war question; apolitical people typically decline to side.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Contested partisan issue on which the stance is neutral by definition.

abortion-legal.rationale: Contested partisan issue on which the stance is neutral by definition.

more-religion-public.rationale: Anabaptist separation favours religion apart from state, Epicureans were sceptical of religion in public life; no unified view.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: A partisan program question; apolitical people do not commit either way.

gradual-change.rationale: Pace of change is a political position; apolitical people take none, though they lean to quiet life.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: No apolitical position on international institutions.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Pacifist Anabaptist strands reject force while Epicurean strands are indifferent, so adherents split.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: A partisan policy dispute; apolitical people neither back nor oppose it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Apoliticism withdraws from political struggle, and Epicurean tranquility (SEP) discourages turmoil, so revolution is mildly rejected.

experts-over-public.rationale: Apolitical people often defer to neutral institutions, but nothing in the stance settles it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Partisan tax question with no apolitical position.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Radical economic change is not an apolitical concern.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No apolitical position on state-organised bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: The apolitical stance is antipathy to political affiliations (Wikipedia definition), which a ruling-party state would demand people embrace.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Form of government is not an apolitical concern; neutral head-of-state ideals fit some, not all.

democracy-best.rationale: Apolitical people abstain from regime debates and may be split between indifference and apathy toward voting.

direct-votes.rationale: Direct votes demand more political participation, which apolitical adherents are reluctant to give (political apathy).

natural-rulers.rationale: Epicurus rested justice on compact rather than natural rank (KD 33), but apolitical adherents are not committed against rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Anabaptist nonresistance forbids violence in every circumstance, and Epicurean tranquility disfavours it, but strands vary.

separate-church-state.rationale: Anabaptist apoliticism sharply separated Christian communities from the state (Wikipedia, Schleitheim), though other strands do not care.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence posture is not an apolitical concern.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land claims are a live partisan cause, and apolitical people neither back nor oppose it.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Epicurean ethics treats each person's own pleasure and tranquility as the aim, though it is hedonism with friendship, not egoism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Epicurus grounds justice in mutual advantage rather than civic duty, and recommends withdrawal from public service.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Whether nature has intrinsic value is environmental philosophy; Epicurean naturalism does not decide it for apolitical adherents.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is a policy dispute that withdrawal from politics leaves open.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: A civilizational critique of industry is an ideological claim apolitical people do not usually make or reject.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological acceleration is a programme of the technology-focused ideologies, not of apoliticism.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is a bioethics question the stance leaves to individuals.

restore-past-order.rationale: Restoration versus progress is a reactionary-progressive divide that apolitical people decline to join.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Apoliticism is defined by antipathy toward political affiliations and being without political bias (Collins quoted in Wikipedia), so judging by results over ideology is natural. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

direct-action.rationale: Apolitical stance withdraws from activism of all kinds, including protest.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative method is an activist doctrine; apolitical people do not engage in movement strategy.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitivist claims are unrelated to the apolitical stance, although Epicurean simplicity is a faint echo.

harm-principle.rationale: Epicurus defines natural justice as a compact neither to harm nor be harmed (KD 31), close to limiting restrictions to preventing harm. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individual versus group rights is a liberal-communitarian dispute apolitical sources leave open.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Withdrawal resembles exit, yet apolitical people do not hold this theory of checks.

positive-liberty.rationale: A debate within liberal theory that apolitical adherents do not weigh in on.

media-academia-power.rationale: A populist claim about institutions; apolitical people may suspect it or ignore it.

hereditarian-race.rationale: A scientific-racial claim with no connection to the apolitical stance.

total-state.rationale: A state directing every area of life is the opposite of retreat from politics; Schleitheim also demands separation from civil affairs.

national-rebirth.rationale: Mass political mobilisation for national renewal conflicts with the stance's disengagement.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A feudal theory of authority with no bearing on apolitical sources.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is a feudal institution that apolitical sources do not defend or attack.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Apoliticism claims neutrality is possible; the claim that all is political is the Gramscian criticism it faces.

universal-morality.rationale: Epicureans were naturalist hedonists who treated justice as conventional (KD 33), but apoliticism has no unified moral theory.

single-common-good.rationale: Epicurean justice is mutual agreement between parties, not a single reasoned common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: A Zionist claim; apolitical people decline to take national sides.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding design is a narrow partisan policy dispute.

economic-freedom.rationale: A classical-liberal claim linking freedoms; apolitical sources do not argue it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Epicureans valued reason and empiricism but Anabaptist apolitical strands are faith-based.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is a partisan welfare design question.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: A futurist avant-garde demand with no link to apoliticism.

workers-nation.rationale: A national-socialist or nationalist labour question the stance leaves alone.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: A culture-war question on which apolitical people decline to commit.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury law is a religious-economic question with no apolitical doctrine.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: No apolitical doctrine; the stance's neutrality does not endorse any such law, but adherents would not campaign against it either.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist theory of the state is the kind of political theorising apolitical people avoid.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Assimilation policy is a nationalist-multiculturalist dispute apolitical people leave open.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracist claim that apolitical sources neither endorse nor reject.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral design is a detail the stance leaves to others.

national-mission.rationale: Missions to spread a government form entail political crusading, opposite to apolitical disengagement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Antipathy toward political affiliations and alienation from leaders (Wikipedia, political apathy) make distrust of elites a common apolitical attitude. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: A postcolonial historical-political judgement that apolitical people stay out of.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious-cultural law proposal outside apolitical sources.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Epicurus treats justice as a compact for mutual non-harm (KD 33), which is not a theory of political legitimacy, and apolitical people seldom take a position on it.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are a question about political affiliation rules rather than apolitical belief.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is a topic apolitical sources do not treat.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined party of revolutionaries is the opposite of apoliticism's antipathy to political affiliations.

priority-to-poor.rationale: A moral-political priority rule with no apolitical source position.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour-law design is a narrow partisan question.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is among reforms proposed to counter apathy (Wikipedia), but no apolitical canon endorses it.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party politicisation of the army conflicts with the neutral-institution ideal behind apoliticism (Peel, Reith examples in Wikipedia).

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A populist-left rule on pay that apolitical sources do not consider.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Antipathy toward political affiliations rejects binding party membership.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: European integration is a partisan dispute apolitical people avoid.

clerical-rule.rationale: Schleitheim says Christians should not hold magisterial office and should stay apart from civil affairs, so religious officials ruling is rejected.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall requires voter engagement, which the stance neither promotes nor opposes explicitly.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: A radical housing proposal with no connection to apoliticism.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not an apolitical doctrine.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum content is a culture-war dispute the stance leaves open.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Obscenity law is a moral-political question the stance does not settle.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: An anti-colonial doctrine unrelated to apolitical sources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Defence doctrine is outside apolitical sources.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate among Marxists that the stance does not enter.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation policy is not an apolitical topic.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: An international-law judgement apolitical sources stay out of.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Apoliticism includes the ideal of impartial institutions standing above party, as with the BBC and civilian policing examples in Wikipedia. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

mixed-constitution.rationale: A classical constitutional theory (Polybius, Aristotle) apolitical sources do not endorse.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is a theory apolitical sources do not endorse or reject.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Majoritarian populism versus constitutionalism is a partisan question the stance leaves open.

moral-incentives.rationale: A Guevarist labour-motivation idea unrelated to the stance.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Both armed revolutionary politics and force are rejected by the stance; Schleitheim forbids weapons of force.

public-money-creation.rationale: A monetary-reform proposal apolitical sources do not consider.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional entrenchment is a design question the apolitical sources do not treat.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Epicurean justice is a compact neither to harm nor be harmed (KD 31) and Schleitheim forbids force entirely, though neither states it as absolute.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Epicurus advises avoiding politics and the general fray, and praises a quiet private life withdrawn from the multitude.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Nothing in withdrawal from politics bears on divorce law; adherents are split or indifferent.

job-guarantee.rationale: Withdrawal from politics gives no view; adherents split between indifference and self-reliance.

democratic-peace.rationale: The apolitical are uninterested in foreign-policy theories, so neutral.

non-intervention.rationale: Indifference to politics gives no view on intervention; Anabaptist nonresistance leans against force but is not specific.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Those uninterested in politics have no stake in this; neutral.

local-production.rationale: Epicurus favoured simple living, but there is no stated view on where goods are produced.

religious-nation.rationale: Anabaptists separate the believing community from the state, so they reject defining the nation by religion; Epicureans are indifferent.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The stance concerns participation, so apolitical adherents are indifferent to how states relate to a leading power.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Indifferent: apoliticism is not about property, though Epicurean and Anabaptist strands each had their own private arrangements.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Indifferent: how public services are run is a political question that apolitical people leave aside.

religion-illusion.rationale: Split: Epicurus held that fear of the gods is a delusion to be dispelled, while the Anabaptist strand was devoutly religious.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Indifferent: language policy is a political question that apolitical people set aside.

majority-settlement.rationale: Indifferent: state settlement policy is a political question left aside by apoliticism.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The stance gives no view on empire; adherents would be indifferent or split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: An activist framework the stance neither endorses nor opposes.

assisted-dying.rationale: Epicurus treated death as nothing to us but gave no policy; adherents are split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Culture-war question outside a stance of non-engagement.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Anabaptists held to God's authority while Epicureans denied divine governance, so adherents are split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Schleitheim rejects the sword for believers but not for the world's magistrates; Epicurean withdrawal is indifferent, so split.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Sovereign debt politics is exactly the kind of partisan dispute the apolitical decline to join.

property-franchise.rationale: The stance concerns whether to participate, not who may vote; adherents are indifferent.

domination-women-nature.rationale: This is a programmatic theory of oppression, which the apolitical stance leaves aside.

open-government-data.rationale: No doctrine on government transparency; the political apathy literature proposes openness as a remedy but adherents do not demand it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Marriage law is a partisan culture-war issue on which the apolitical take no side.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Epicurus' Principal Doctrines treat justice as a compact of mutual non-harm for security, so some means of protection is kept, though adherents avoid politics. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

vote-delegation.rationale: Apathy toward politics means little interest in delegating votes; adherents are indifferent rather than opposed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Apolitical adherents have no stake in the question of the basis of income.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Apolitical adherents have no stake in national identity narratives.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Epicureans deny politics is a cosmic struggle while Anabaptists see a struggle of the world against the church, so adherents are split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Apolitical adherents have no stake in diaspora questions.

culture-before-state.rationale: Apolitical adherents have no stake in the order of national projects.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Apolitical adherents have no stake in minority-majority economic questions.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Apolitical adherents have no stake in territorial administration.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Apoliticism gives no view on local public services; adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Anabaptists were deeply religious while Epicureans were materialist, so adherents are split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate electorates are a partisan constitutional dispute the apolitical decline to join, though Anabaptist separatism and a wish to avoid politics point both ways.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Apolitical people tend to distrust political claims on both sides; no doctrine either way, so adherents are split.

future-generations.rationale: Epicurean and Anabaptist withdrawal gives no doctrine on duties to the unborn; adherents split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Epicurus valued security from others but the stance has no arms policy; Anabaptist nonresistance leans toward reduction while apathetic citizens are indifferent, so it is split.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Open diplomacy is a policy position; apolitical people are uninterested in it, though distrust of leaders gives a slight pull toward openness.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Anabaptists reject the sword while Epicureans and the merely apathetic make no stand; adherents are split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Withdrawal from civic loyalties, as in Schleitheim's separation from the world and Epicurean retreat, runs against treating the nation as sacred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Epicurus has a view of human nature but the apolitical stance has no stake in rights grounded on it; adherents are split.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Withdrawal from politics gives no view on religious truth; Epicurean and Anabaptist strands differ.

voter-id.rationale: Electoral rules are an ordinary party-political dispute that the apolitical decline to join.

premarital-sex.rationale: Personal morality is outside the stance; adherents are split between permissive and traditional views.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Apolitical people take no position on state security powers; adherents are split.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is a partisan policy question the apolitical decline to take a side on.

women-suffrage.rationale: The stance does not address who may vote; it concerns declining to take part, so adherents are split.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: No doctrine on religion's social effects; adherents are split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Government equality policy is a partisan matter on which apolitical people take no side.

simple-living.rationale: Epicurus held that natural wealth is limited and easily obtained and counselled a quiet life of few desires, which the Epicurean strand of apoliticism carries.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment is an ordinary political dispute that apolitical people take no side on.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy is a standard partisan fight; withdrawal means no committed position.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Welfare design is a partisan question that apolitical people decline to take a side on.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Business regulation is a partisan economic question the stance is indifferent to.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Withdrawal from politics gives no view on how wealth should be judged; adherents are split between indifference and Epicurean self-reliance.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Adherents are split: Epicurean prudence counsels obeying law to keep tranquility, while the Anabaptist tradition places conscience above the state.

material-over-identity.rationale: Apolitical people neither join the left nor weigh its priorities.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Welfare cuts are a partisan question; no apolitical doctrine settles it. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A good life is best lived withdrawn from public affairs rather than taking part in politics.
missingStatements.rationale: Epicurus advises avoiding politics and the general fray, and praises a quiet private life withdrawn from the multitude.

missingStatements.text: Police, broadcasters and other public bodies should stay strictly impartial between political parties.
missingStatements.rationale: Wikipedia cites Peel's civilian policing and the BBC's Reithian impartiality as institutional forms of apolitical neutrality.

notes: Apoliticism is a stance on participation, so most policy answers are neutral and low-confidence; Epicurean and Anabaptist strands differ (Epicureans accept the state as useful compact, Anabaptists reject force). It may fail the inclusion check, which is an honest result.
